To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
functional food and/or supplement use is not widespread in the Netherlands and that the determinants of functional foods and supplements use differ by type of product.

(i) the number of functional food and supplement daily consumers in the Netherlands was low, (ii) determinants of functional foods and supplements differed per type, and (iii) consumers were more likely to use functional foods and supplements when they had a poorer subjective health or were smokers.

the consumption of functional foods or dietary supplements is relatively low in the general Dutch population, but that consumers are more likely to be male, to be older and better educated, to smoke, and to report poor subjective health.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and description of functional food and/or supplement consumers.
the characteristics of consumers, not with effects of functional food and supplement intake.
a relatively small group of consumers, but it provides some insight into the characteristics of this group.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the consumption of functional foods or dietary supplements is not a healthy lifestyle per se. Functional foods and/or supplements are food or food ingredients that provide a specific physiological benefit beyond basic nutrition.
functional foods are not used by the majority of the population, but that there is a subgroup of consumers who use them, and that the characteristics of these consumers are product-specific.
the majority of Dutch functional food consumers and/or dietary supplement users are relatively healthy individuals, with a healthy diet, a high level of education, and a healthy lifestyle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
consumers of cholesterol-lowering products are more likely to be smokers and to report a poorer subjective health.
functional foods and supplements are used by a relatively low percentage of the Dutch population and that the characteristics of consumers differ according to type of product.
the consumption of functional foods or dietary supplements is low, but is related to lifestyle factors, such as smoking and vegetable consumption, and to subjective health.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumption of functional food and supplements is not widespread in The Netherlands.
the use of dietary supplements is associated with the consumption of functional foods and that both are related to lifestyle factors.
the determinants of functional foods and supplement use are product specific, so generalisation is not legitimate.
